newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish t-bill yields seen easing in short-term.
newsitem.headline: Turkish t-bill yields seen easing in short-term.

text.p: Turkish treasury-bill yields may ease further in coming days despite political and economic instability and a planned withholding tax on government borrowing papers, bankers said on Wednesday.
Bankers said demand for the treasury bills, particularly for those with 1997 maturities continued.
"Despite some negative developments, the treasury's record t-bill sale was very succesful at lower yields," said Ali Ozenc, cash flow manager at private Finansbank.
"There was demand for the papers as the treasury has no debt repayment until October 30," he told Reuters.
He said the plan for a 10 percent withholding tax on t-bill earnings also contributed to the present demand rise.
The treasury sold a record 288 trillion lira worth of a 238 day t-bills at an average yield of 130.72 on Tuesday, down from 131.20 percent at the previous 217-day auction on October 1.
Demand for the auction was also at an all-time record level with 480.6 trillion lira.

Paper demand at t-bill auctions have been rising since the government announced three weeks ago that it would introduce a 10 percent withholding tax on interest income from t-bills and bonds with 1997 maturities three weeks ago.

Bankers said demand for t-bills had risen because the treasury has annouced that the new tax would not be retroactive after it takes effect. The government has yet to issue a decree to implement the withholding tax plan.
The treasury has successfully extended its borrowing maturity up to eight months in the last three auctions.
"Banks make profits from t-bill trading and expect further gains as t-bill yields ease. So their demand for the papers is increasing," said Sadk Can Ipek, Garanti Yatirim Bank treasurer.
Ipek said Tuesday's t-bill auction might be the last chance to buy t-bills before the 10 percent withholding tax takes effect. He said foreign investors were also buying t-bills.
In the last six auctions since September 3, the treasury drained a total of 642 trillion lira, while injecting 578 trillion lira from t-bill maturities.
Average t-bill yields gradually rose by 13 points to 130.72 percent on Tuesday, from 117.50 percent on September 3.
Last month, the treasury sold $1.12 billion worth foreign currency-denominated paper in the domestic market.
The treasury has no debt repayment until end-October. But it will repay 471.5 trillion lira of t-bills in the first 20 days of November.
